skills.name: Menu engineering & recipe costing
skills.one_liner: Kasavana-Smith stars, plowhorses, puzzles and dogs, with plate costs and price moves.
skills.description: Costs every recipe to the plate, using as-purchased versus edible-portion yields and current invoice prices, then plots the menu on the Kasavana-Smith matrix (stars, plowhorses, puzzles, dogs) from real sales mix and contribution margin. Each item gets a specific action: reprice, re-engineer the recipe, reposition on the menu, or remove.
skills.when: food cost is creeping up, the menu is being redesigned or repriced, or the owner does not know which dishes make money

inputs.label: Item sales counts for a representative period
inputs.fallback_example: POS item sales report for the period (CSV or PDF)

inputs.label: Recent supplier invoices or price lists
inputs.example: Photos of this month's produce and meat invoices

inputs.label: Target food cost percentage and constraints
inputs.example: Under 30 percent; keep the burger under $18

outputs.name: Recipe costing and menu matrix
outputs.description: Plate cost per item with yields, food cost %, contribution margin, menu mix % and quadrant, all with formulas.

outputs.name: Menu engineering matrix
outputs.description: Popularity versus contribution margin scatter with quadrant lines.

outputs.name: Menu actions
outputs.description: Per item: quadrant, action, new price or recipe change, and expected margin impact.

skills.instructions: 1. Read item sales for a representative period with connector_read (or file_parse on the owner's export when nothing is connected) (or a POS export), excluding holidays and one-off events. 2. Parse recipes with file_parse and read invoice photos with vision_describe to get current unit prices; convert units and apply yield factors (as-purchased to edible portion) so trim and cooking loss are costed. 3. In code_interpreter compute plate cost, food cost %, and contribution margin (price minus plate cost) per item. 4. Classify with Kasavana-Smith: popularity is high if an item's menu mix is at least 70 percent of an equal share (0.7 / number of items in the category); margin is high if its contribution margin is at least the category's weighted average. Stars are high on both, plowhorses are popular with low margin, puzzles have high margin but low popularity, and dogs are low on both. 5. Recommend actions: stars keep and protect; plowhorses re-engineer the recipe or portion, or make a modest price increase; puzzles reposition, rename, describe better or feature; dogs remove or rework. Model the margin impact of each price move with a conservative volume assumption. 6. Build the costing workbook with spreadsheet_generate, the matrix with chart_generate and the action brief with document_generate. 7. State what could not be verified, such as recipes that are not followed as written or invoice prices that change weekly.

workflow.title: Read sales mix
workflow.brief: Read item-level sales for a representative period.
workflow.acceptance: Sales mix by item and category, or an export requested.

workflow.title: Recipes and invoices
workflow.brief: Parse recipes and read invoice prices.
workflow.acceptance: Every menu item has a recipe and every ingredient has a current price, or is flagged.

workflow.title: Cost and classify
workflow.brief: Compute plate cost with yields, contribution margin and quadrants.
workflow.acceptance: Formulas shown; every item classified.

workflow.title: Recommend actions
workflow.brief: Recommend an action and price or recipe change per item with margin impact.
workflow.acceptance: Every item has an action; impact assumptions stated.

workflow.title: Numbers audit
workflow.brief: A cost and margin analyst re-derives a sample of plate costs and quadrants.
workflow.acceptance: First line is APPROVED or CHANGES; costing errors corrected.

workflow.title: Render workbook, chart and brief
workflow.brief: Render the costing workbook, matrix chart and action brief.
workflow.acceptance: Numbers agree across all three.

quality_checks.criterion: Plate costs use current invoice prices and yield factors.
Quadrant thresholds follow Kasavana-Smith (70 percent popularity rule, weighted-average margin).
Every recommendation shows its expected margin impact and assumption.
Holiday and event periods are excluded from the sales mix.
Items are compared within their category (starters with starters).

skills.example_request: Our food costs crept up to 36% and I don't know which dishes are killing us. Cost our menu and tell me what to reprice, promote or cut.

skills.name: Prime cost & labor scheduling
skills.one_liner: Prime cost tracking and a labor schedule matched to covers.
skills.description: A weekly prime cost tracker (cost of goods from inventory counts plus total labor including taxes and benefits, as a share of sales) and a labor schedule matched to forecast covers by daypart. It uses sales per labor hour and labor standards, flags overtime and scheduling-rule risks, and produces a draft schedule the manager can adjust.
skills.when: labor or food cost is out of line, weekday and weekend staffing feel wrong, or the owner wants a weekly cost discipline

inputs.label: Sales and covers by day and hour
inputs.fallback_example: POS sales and covers by day and hour (CSV)

inputs.label: Hours, wages and payroll costs
inputs.fallback_example: payroll summary and timesheet exports (CSV or PDF)

inputs.label: Target prime cost and local scheduling rules
inputs.example: Prime cost under 62 percent; no clopens

outputs.name: Prime cost tracker
outputs.description: Weekly COGS (beginning + purchases - ending inventory), labor with burden, sales, prime cost %.

outputs.name: Draft labor schedule
outputs.description: Shifts by role and daypart matched to forecast covers, with labor % and SPLH.

outputs.name: Labor and prime cost memo
outputs.description: Where the money goes, the moves to make, and compliance flags to confirm.

skills.instructions: 1. Read sales, covers, hours and payroll with connector_read (or file_parse on the owner's export when nothing is connected); parse inventory counts and purchases with file_parse. 2. Compute weekly prime cost in code_interpreter: COGS (beginning inventory + purchases - ending inventory) plus total labor including payroll taxes and benefits, divided by sales. Show the trend against the owner's target and label any industry benchmark as a benchmark. 3. Forecast covers by weekday and daypart from 12 weeks of history (weekday averages with trend and known events), and show the error range. 4. Set labor standards per role (for example covers per server-hour, and prep hours per 100 covers), then build a draft schedule that matches staffing to forecast, respects availability and certifications, and reports labor % and sales per labor hour per shift. 5. Flag, for the owner to confirm with an HR professional: overtime, break rules, minor labor rules, and predictive-scheduling or fair-workweek ordinances where they apply. 6. Build the tracker and schedule with spreadsheet_generate, charts with chart_generate and the memo with document_generate; ask the owner to approve schedule principles with request_owner_decision. Publishing the schedule to staff is the manager's action. 7. State what could not be verified, such as the accuracy of inventory counts or forecast accuracy during unusual weeks.

workflow.title: Read sales, covers and labor
workflow.brief: Read sales, covers, hours and payroll for 12 weeks.
workflow.acceptance: Complete weekly data, or gaps listed.

workflow.title: Prime cost and forecast
workflow.brief: Compute weekly prime cost and forecast covers by daypart.
workflow.acceptance: Prime cost formula shown; forecast includes an error range.

workflow.title: Owner sets principles
workflow.brief: Decision card: targets, labor standards and scheduling rules.
workflow.acceptance: Owner approves or edits standards.

workflow.title: Draft schedule
workflow.brief: Build the draft schedule to forecast within standards and availability.
workflow.acceptance: Every shift has a role and reason; labor % per day shown; flags listed.

workflow.title: Operator review
workflow.brief: An operations reviewer checks feasibility, coverage and fairness of shifts.
workflow.acceptance: First line is APPROVED or CHANGES; uncovered peaks or unfair patterns flagged.

workflow.title: Tracker, schedule and memo
workflow.brief: Render the tracker, schedule and memo.
workflow.acceptance: Numbers agree across files.

quality_checks.criterion: Labor cost includes payroll taxes and benefits.
Scheduling-law and overtime risks are flagged for the owner to confirm, never assumed compliant.
The schedule is a draft; publishing it is the manager's action.
Forecasts show an error range.
Benchmarks are labelled as benchmarks.

skills.example_request: Labor is eating us alive on weeknights but we're slammed on Saturdays. Build a prime cost tracker and a schedule that matches staff to covers.

skills.name: Property listing & CMA pack
skills.one_liner: Comparative market analysis, listing copy and a fair-housing-aware marketing plan.
skills.description: A listing pack for a residential property: a comparative market analysis from recent sold, pending and active comps with explicit adjustments and a suggested range (labelled a CMA, not an appraisal), listing copy that describes the property rather than who should live there, a photo review, and a fair-housing-aware marketing plan, all for the agent's or broker's review.
skills.when: an agent or owner is preparing to list a property, preparing a listing presentation, or resetting price on a stale listing

inputs.label: Property details, condition and upgrades
inputs.example: 3 bed, 2 bath bungalow, 1,450 sq ft, new roof 2023

inputs.label: MLS export of nearby sold, pending and active listings

outputs.name: CMA workbook
outputs.description: Comps, adjustments with rationale, adjusted values and the suggested range.

outputs.name: Listing presentation
outputs.description: Market snapshot, CMA summary, pricing strategy and marketing plan.

outputs.name: Listing copy and marketing plan
outputs.description: MLS remarks within character limits, feature list, channel plan and timeline.

skills.instructions: 1. Regulated domain (legal): Drafts, issue lists and research only. Never state a legal conclusion as certain, never say it is legal advice, flag jurisdiction assumptions, and add an attorney-review step before anything is signed or sent. Fair-housing advertising rules and, in many US states, price-opinion and CMA rules make this licensee work: the CMA is prepared for a licensed agent's use, and the listing broker reviews everything before anything is published. 2. Parse the comps export with file_parse. Select comparables: sold within about 3-6 months, same neighborhood or submarket, similar size (about 20 percent either way), bed and bath count, age and condition; use pendings and actives for context and expireds as a warning. 3. In code_interpreter make explicit adjustments (size, bedrooms, bathrooms, garage, lot, condition, upgrades) with a rationale for each, then derive a suggested range. Label it clearly as a comparative market analysis, not an appraisal. 4. Check the local market context (inventory, days on market, list-to-sale ratio) with web_search, and cite it. 5. Review photos with vision_describe for order, gaps and quality. Use image_edit only for honest corrections; any virtual staging must be labelled as such, and permanent features are never altered. 6. Write listing copy that describes the property and its amenities, never who should live there: no references to familial status, religion, race, national origin, sex, disability or other protected characteristics, and no steering language. 7. Plan marketing: channels, launch sequence, open houses and a timeline tied to the seller's goals. 8. Build the CMA with spreadsheet_generate, the presentation with deck_generate and the copy and plan with document_generate, for the agent's or broker's review. Disclosure obligations and contract terms are for the broker and an attorney. 9. State what could not be verified, such as interior condition of comps or concessions not shown in the export.

workflow.title: Load comps and photos
workflow.brief: Parse the comps export and review photos.
workflow.acceptance: Comps table loaded; photo notes written.

workflow.title: CMA
workflow.brief: Select comps, adjust with rationale and derive a range.
workflow.acceptance: Each adjustment has a rationale; the range is labelled a CMA, not an appraisal.

workflow.title: Market context
workflow.brief: Research local inventory, days on market and list-to-sale ratio.
workflow.acceptance: At least two cited market indicators.

workflow.title: Copy and marketing plan
workflow.brief: Write listing copy and the marketing plan.
workflow.acceptance: Copy describes the property only; plan has a dated timeline.

workflow.title: Fair-housing and accuracy review
workflow.brief: A reviewer checks copy and plan for fair-housing risks and the CMA for errors.
workflow.acceptance: First line is APPROVED or CHANGES; any steering or protected-class language removed.

workflow.title: Licensed review by the listing broker
workflow.brief: The listing broker (and an attorney for any contract or disclosure question) reviews the CMA, copy and plan before anything is published.
workflow.acceptance: Broker sign-off recorded with changes applied; nothing published before it.

workflow.title: Render pack
workflow.brief: Render the CMA workbook, listing presentation and copy.
workflow.acceptance: Pack renders; numbers agree across files.

quality_checks.criterion: The listing broker reviews the CMA, copy and plan before anything is published, and the CMA is labelled for a licensed agent's use.
Listing copy describes the property, never the kind of buyer, and avoids protected-class and steering language.
The price analysis is labelled a CMA, not an appraisal.
Virtual staging or edits are disclosed; permanent features are never altered.
Every comp adjustment has a stated rationale.
Market context is cited.

skills.example_request: I'm listing a 3-bed bungalow on Maple Street next week. Pull together the CMA from these MLS comps, write the listing and plan the marketing — nothing that'll get me in trouble with fair housing.

skills.name: Construction estimate & bid package
skills.one_liner: Quantity takeoff, cost estimate, bid package and change-order log.
skills.description: A bid-ready estimate: quantity takeoff from the drawings by CSI MasterFormat division, unit costs from the contractor's own history and leveled sub or supplier quotes, labor productivity, overhead, profit and contingency markups, and explicit alternates, exclusions and clarifications. It also includes a CPM schedule and a change-order log for the job.
skills.when: a contractor is bidding a job from drawings and specs, or needs to price a change order or re-baseline an estimate

inputs.label: Plan set, specs and addenda
inputs.example: Architectural and MEP PDFs for a 2,400 sq ft fit-out

inputs.label: Historical unit costs, crew rates and productivity
Overhead, profit, contingency, bond and insurance rates
inputs.example: 10 percent overhead, 8 percent profit, 5 percent contingency

inputs.label: Bid form, due date and instructions

outputs.name: Estimate workbook
outputs.description: Takeoff, unit costs, labor, subs, markups and summary by division, with formulas.

outputs.name: Bid package
outputs.description: Proposal letter, scope by division, inclusions, exclusions, alternates, clarifications and schedule of values.

outputs.name: CPM schedule
outputs.description: Critical-path Gantt of major activities.

outputs.name: Change-order log
outputs.description: Log with pricing method, status and schedule impact.

skills.instructions: 1. Parse specs, bid instructions and addenda with file_parse; read plan sheets with vision_describe, confirming the drawing scale on each sheet before measuring. Read project history from Procore with connector_read if enabled. 2. Do the quantity takeoff by CSI MasterFormat division (areas, lengths, counts), with waste factors stated and every quantity referenced to its sheet. 3. Price from the contractor's own unit costs and productivity rates; never invent a unit price. Where no cost exists, mark an allowance for the owner to confirm. 4. Level subcontractor and supplier quotes in a bid tabulation: scope gaps, exclusions and apples-to-apples totals. 5. Apply the owner's markups (overhead, profit, contingency, bond and insurance) in code_interpreter and reconcile totals; list alternates, exclusions and clarifications. 6. Draft a CPM schedule of major activities with diagram_generate, and a change-order log template with pricing method (lump sum, unit price, time and materials) and triggers. 7. Ask the owner to confirm allowances and markups with request_owner_decision, then build the workbook with spreadsheet_generate and the bid package with document_generate. 8. Structural, life-safety and code-compliance questions go to the design professionals of record and the building official; the estimate is not an engineering judgement. State what could not be verified, such as quantities on sheets that were unclear or out of scale.

workflow.title: Read the documents
workflow.brief: Parse specs and addenda and read plan sheets with their scales.
workflow.acceptance: Sheet index with scale per sheet and addenda listed.

workflow.title: Quantity takeoff
workflow.brief: Take off quantities by division with waste factors and sheet references.
workflow.acceptance: Every quantity cites a sheet; waste factors stated.

workflow.title: Price and level bids
workflow.brief: Price from owner costs, level sub quotes and apply markups.
workflow.acceptance: No invented unit prices; allowances flagged; totals reconcile.

workflow.title: Owner confirms allowances and markups
workflow.brief: Decision card with allowances, markups and bid-level choices.
workflow.acceptance: Owner confirms or edits.

workflow.title: Schedule and change-order log
workflow.brief: Draft the CPM schedule and change-order log.
workflow.acceptance: Critical path identified; log has pricing methods.

workflow.title: Estimator review
workflow.brief: A second estimator checks quantities, scope gaps and the arithmetic.
workflow.acceptance: First line is APPROVED or CHANGES; scope gaps and errors listed.

workflow.title: Bid package
workflow.brief: Render the estimate workbook and bid package.
workflow.acceptance: Bid package matches the bid form; exclusions and clarifications explicit.

quality_checks.criterion: Every quantity cites its drawing sheet and the scale was confirmed.
No unit price is invented; missing costs are flagged allowances.
Exclusions, alternates and clarifications are explicit.
Sub quotes are leveled for scope before comparison.
Markups match the owner's confirmed rates.

skills.example_request: We're bidding a 2,400 sq ft restaurant fit-out from these drawings, due in 10 days. Do the takeoff and estimate and put together the bid package with our usual markups.

skills.name: Practice front-desk & no-show playbook
skills.one_liner: Scheduling templates, reminders and intake flows. Administrative only, no clinical advice.
skills.description: Administrative playbook for a healthcare practice front desk: scheduling templates by provider and appointment type, a no-show analysis on de-identified aggregate data, a reminder cadence that reveals no health details, waitlist backfill, a no-show policy draft, intake flow design and front-desk scripts. Anything clinical routes to the practice's clinicians.
skills.when: no-shows are high, the phones overwhelm the front desk, schedules have gaps and overbooks, or intake is slow and paper-heavy

inputs.label: De-identified appointment history: type, day, time, lead time, status
inputs.example: Last 6 months, no names or diagnoses
inputs.fallback_example: de-identified appointment export with type, day, time and status only (CSV)

inputs.label: Providers, appointment types and durations
inputs.example: Three physiotherapists; initial 45 min, follow-up 30 min

inputs.label: Current reminders, policies and intake forms
Clinician-approved prep or intake questions, used verbatim

outputs.name: Scheduling templates
outputs.description: Weekly templates per provider with slot types, buffers and same-day slots.

outputs.name: Front-desk playbook
outputs.description: Reminder cadence, waitlist backfill, scripts, escalation rules and a no-show policy draft.

outputs.name: Intake form design
outputs.description: Administrative intake flow with clinician-supplied questions inserted verbatim.

outputs.name: Patient flow
outputs.description: From booking to check-out, with handoffs.

skills.instructions: 1. Read appointment history with connector_read (or file_parse on the owner's export when nothing is connected) in de-identified, aggregate form (type, day, time, lead time, reminder status, outcome); never pull names, diagnoses or clinical notes. 2. In code_interpreter find no-show drivers by day, time, lead time, appointment type and reminder status, and estimate the revenue lost. 3. Design scheduling templates per provider: slot types and durations, buffers, same-day slots, and a controlled overbook only where the data supports it. 4. Set a reminder cadence (for example 72 hours, 24 hours and 2 hours, with confirm or reschedule links) whose messages include date, time, location and provider only, with no diagnosis, procedure or other health detail. Add waitlist backfill for cancellations. SMS or WhatsApp goes only to contacts with documented consent for this purpose; respect quiet hours, include STOP opt-out in every message, keep transactional and marketing messages separate, and flag the consent basis per region (TCPA and CTIA in the US, PECR and GDPR in the UK and EU) for the owner to confirm. 5. Draft the no-show and cancellation policy, and front-desk scripts for booking and rescheduling. Any clinical question, symptom or medication question is routed to the clinical team; urgent symptoms get the practice's emergency instruction. 6. Design the intake flow with web_page_generate using only clinician-supplied clinical questions, verbatim; draw the patient flow with diagram_generate; build templates with spreadsheet_generate and the playbook with document_generate. 7. Regulated domain (medical_clinical): Administrative and non-clinical work only. No diagnosis, treatment, triage or dosing guidance; route anything clinical to the practice's clinicians; minimize protected health information. Escalate to a licensed clinician (licensed review) before anything leaves the workspace; never present the output as professional advice and never imply a licence you do not hold. 8. Ask the owner with request_owner_decision to have a clinician approve any patient-facing text with clinical content, and to confirm privacy and consent requirements for texting. State what could not be verified.

workflow.title: Read de-identified appointment data
workflow.brief: Read aggregate appointment history without names or clinical details.
workflow.acceptance: Dataset contains no names, diagnoses or notes.

workflow.title: No-show drivers
workflow.brief: Analyse no-shows by day, time, lead time, type and reminder status.
workflow.acceptance: Drivers ranked with counts and lost revenue estimate.

workflow.title: Templates, reminders and scripts
workflow.brief: Design templates, reminder cadence, backfill, policy and scripts.
workflow.acceptance: Reminders contain no health details; clinical questions route to clinicians.

workflow.title: Render templates, playbook, form and flow
workflow.brief: Render the templates, playbook, intake form and patient flow.
workflow.acceptance: All outputs render; intake form uses clinician text verbatim.

workflow.title: Privacy and operations review
workflow.brief: A privacy-minded reviewer checks minimum-necessary data and message content; an operations reviewer checks feasibility.
workflow.acceptance: First line is APPROVED or CHANGES; any health detail in messages removed.

workflow.title: Licensed review
workflow.brief: Raise a decision card (request_owner_decision) asking the owner to route the draft to a licensed clinician. The clinician approves all patient-facing text with clinical content; the owner confirms texting consent requirements.
workflow.acceptance: Owner confirms the licensed reviewer has approved, or returns their changes; nothing external happens before this step completes.

quality_checks.criterion: The medical_clinical rule is restated and the work is routed to a licensed clinician for licensed review before anything is sent, signed or published.
No names, diagnoses or clinical notes are used in the analysis.
Reminder messages contain no diagnosis, procedure or other health detail.
Front-desk scripts route every clinical question to the clinical team.
Templates are based on the practice's own no-show and demand data.

SMS or WhatsApp goes only to contacts with documented consent for this purpose, respects quiet hours, offers STOP opt-out in every message, separates transactional from marketing messages, and flags the consent basis per region.

skills.example_request: Our physio clinic has a 14% no-show rate and the front desk is drowning in phone calls. Fix our scheduling templates, reminders and intake so the day runs smoothly.

skills.name: Law firm intake & conflict-check workflow
skills.one_liner: Intake form, conflict-check steps and engagement hand-off. Operations only.
skills.description: Operations design for a law firm's front door: an intake form and practice-area triage, a conflict-check procedure (every party, alias and entity checked against firm records, then cleared by an attorney), intake scripts that give no legal advice, attorney-approved engagement and declination hand-offs, and speed-to-lead and conversion metrics.
skills.when: a firm loses leads to slow or messy intake, conflicts are checked inconsistently, or the firm is setting up a practice-management tool

inputs.label: Practice areas and matters the firm takes or declines
inputs.example: Family law and estate planning; no criminal matters

inputs.label: How intake and conflict checks happen now

outputs.name: Intake form
outputs.description: Prospect details, matter type, all parties and aliases, key dates mentioned, and how they heard of the firm.

outputs.name: Intake and conflict-check SOP
outputs.description: Steps, owners, timings, attorney sign-off points and records to keep.

outputs.name: Intake workflow
outputs.description: From first contact to engagement or declination.

outputs.name: Scripts and hand-off templates
outputs.description: Intake scripts and engagement or declination templates marked for attorney approval.

skills.instructions: 1. Map the current process and read how matters and contacts are structured in the practice-management system with connector_read if enabled; parse existing templates with file_parse. 2. Design the intake form with web_page_generate: prospect, matter type, all adverse and related parties with aliases and entity names, key dates the prospect mentions (flagged for an attorney, never calculated as deadlines), referral source, and consent to be contacted. Collect only what intake needs. 3. Write the conflict-check procedure: search every party and alias against clients, matters and past prospects; record results; an attorney clears or declines; no substantive discussion before clearance. 4. Write intake scripts that gather facts without giving legal advice or evaluating the case, and route urgent matters to an attorney promptly. 5. Draft engagement and declination hand-off templates marked for attorney approval, and draw the workflow with diagram_generate. 6. Define metrics (speed to first response, consult-booked rate, conversion, conflicts found) in a tracker built with spreadsheet_generate, and render the SOP with document_generate. 7. Regulated domain (legal): Drafts, issue lists and research only. Never state a legal conclusion as certain, never say it is legal advice, flag jurisdiction assumptions, and add an attorney-review step before anything is signed or sent. Escalate to a licensed attorney in the relevant jurisdiction (licensed review) before anything leaves the workspace; never present the output as professional advice and never imply a licence you do not hold. 8. Ask the owner with request_owner_decision to route the SOP and templates to the firm's supervising attorney. State what could not be verified, such as how the firm's system matches names and aliases.

workflow.title: Map current system
workflow.brief: Read matter and contact structures and parse existing templates.
workflow.acceptance: Current fields and gaps listed.

workflow.title: Design intake and conflict procedure
workflow.brief: Design the form, conflict-check steps, scripts and templates.
workflow.acceptance: Conflict check covers all parties and aliases; scripts contain no legal advice.

workflow.title: Render form, SOP, workflow and tracker
workflow.brief: Render the intake form, SOP, workflow diagram and metrics tracker.
workflow.acceptance: Every attorney sign-off point is marked.

workflow.title: Legal operations review
workflow.brief: A legal operations reviewer checks completeness, data minimization and sign-off points.
workflow.acceptance: First line is APPROVED or CHANGES; missing sign-offs flagged.

workflow.title: Licensed review
workflow.brief: Raise a decision card (request_owner_decision) asking the owner to route the draft to a licensed attorney in the relevant jurisdiction. The supervising attorney approves the conflict procedure, scripts and templates.
workflow.acceptance: Owner confirms the licensed reviewer has approved, or returns their changes; nothing external happens before this step completes.

quality_checks.criterion: The legal rule is restated and the work is routed to a licensed attorney in the relevant jurisdiction for licensed review before anything is sent, signed or published.
Intake scripts never give legal advice or evaluate the merits of a case.
Conflicts are cleared by an attorney before any substantive discussion.
Deadlines mentioned by prospects are flagged for an attorney, never calculated.
The form collects only what intake needs.

skills.example_request: Our small family-law firm loses leads because intake is a mess of sticky notes, and we nearly missed a conflict last month. Design an intake and conflict-check workflow for Clio.

skills.name: Agency SOW & scope guardrails
skills.one_liner: Scoped SOW, assumptions, change-order triggers and retainer health checks.
skills.description: A tightly scoped statement of work: objectives, in and out of scope, deliverables with acceptance criteria, an estimate built from the work breakdown, assumptions and client responsibilities, revision rounds, milestones and explicit change-order triggers. It adds a retainer health check (utilization, realization, effective hourly rate, burn versus plan) so scope creep shows up in numbers.
skills.when: an agency or consultancy is scoping a new project or retainer, or existing retainers feel like unlimited work

inputs.label: Time tracking and billing for current retainers

outputs.name: Statement of work draft
outputs.description: Scope, deliverables, acceptance, assumptions, timeline, change triggers, fees; marked for the owner's attorney before signing.

outputs.name: Estimate and retainer health
outputs.description: WBS hours by role, fees, and retainer utilization, realization, effective rate and burn.

outputs.name: Change-order triggers
outputs.description: What counts as out of scope and the change-order process.

skills.instructions: 1. Parse the brief and past SOWs with file_parse; read time and billing data with connector_read if enabled. 2. Build a work breakdown structure to deliverables, estimate hours by role from past actuals (not optimism), and add a stated contingency. 3. Write the SOW: objectives, in scope, explicitly out of scope, deliverables with acceptance criteria, number of revision rounds, client responsibilities and feedback turnaround, milestones, assumptions, fees and payment terms. 4. Define change-order triggers (new deliverables, extra rounds, late client inputs, changed requirements) and a simple change-order process. 5. For existing retainers, compute in code_interpreter utilization (billable over available hours), realization (billed over standard value), effective hourly rate and burn versus plan, and flag unprofitable retainers. 6. Ask the owner to confirm fees and scope boundaries with request_owner_decision, then build the workbook with spreadsheet_generate and the SOW with document_generate. Terms with legal effect go to the owner's attorney before signing. 7. State what could not be verified, such as time data that is incomplete or estimates for work the agency has not done before.

workflow.title: Read brief and history
workflow.brief: Parse the brief, past SOWs and actuals.
workflow.acceptance: Brief requirements listed; historical hours by deliverable type extracted.

workflow.title: WBS and estimate
workflow.brief: Build the WBS and estimate hours and fees from actuals.
workflow.acceptance: Every deliverable has hours by role; contingency stated.

workflow.title: Retainer data
workflow.brief: Read time and billing for current retainers.
workflow.acceptance: Data per retainer, or marked unavailable.

workflow.title: Retainer health
workflow.brief: Compute utilization, realization, effective rate and burn.
workflow.acceptance: Every retainer scored; unprofitable ones flagged.

workflow.title: Draft SOW and triggers
workflow.brief: Draft the SOW and change-order triggers.
workflow.acceptance: Out-of-scope list and acceptance criteria are explicit.

workflow.title: Sceptic review
workflow.brief: Challenge vague scope, optimistic hours and missing client responsibilities.

skills.one_liner: OEE baseline, loss tree and a SMED plan to cut changeover time.
skills.description: Measures OEE (availability x performance x quality) from production logs, breaks losses into a loss tree using the TPM six big losses, and attacks the biggest one: usually changeovers, with a SMED study built from a phone video of a real changeover. Internal steps are separated from external ones, internal work is converted to external, and the result is standard work and a pilot plan.
skills.when: a line or machine underperforms, changeovers are long, or the owner needs capacity without buying equipment

inputs.label: Production logs: planned time, downtime, counts, rejects
Video or photos of a real changeover

outputs.description: From planned time to good output, loss by loss.

outputs.description: Changeover elements, internal versus external, conversions, standard work and a pilot plan.

outputs.description: Pre-changeover, changeover and restart checklists.

skills.instructions: 1. Parse production logs with file_parse and compute in code_interpreter: availability (run time over planned time), performance (ideal cycle time times count over run time), quality (good over total), and OEE, by shift, product and machine. 2. Build a loss tree with the six big losses (breakdowns, setups and adjustments, small stops, reduced speed, startup rejects, production rejects) and a waterfall with chart_generate. 3. For the changeover study, review the video frame by frame with vision_describe (and transcribe operator narration with stt if present); list every element with its duration. 4. Classify each element as internal (machine stopped) or external (can be done while running); convert internal to external (pre-staging tools and materials, preset settings), then streamline the rest (quick-release fasteners, standard heights, parallel work, eliminating adjustments). 5. Write standard work checklists and a pilot plan with a target time and how it will be measured. 6. Never bypass lockout/tagout, guarding or other safety controls; changes to guarding or energy isolation go to the site's safety lead. 7. Build the workbook with spreadsheet_generate and the study with document_generate, and state what could not be verified, such as ideal cycle times the owner estimated or steps hidden from the camera.

Score at-risk members from signals: visit frequency down against their own baseline, missed booked classes, freeze requests, failed payments and upcoming renewal. 4. Design the journey and plays: first-30-day onboarding (a booked first class, a check-in after visit two, a habit goal), mid-life check-ins, save offers (freeze or downgrade) and win-back at 30, 60 and 90 days. 5. Parse the executed contract and every addendum with file_parse. Extract each time-bound obligation with its clause reference: earnest money, due diligence or inspection period, repair request and response, appraisal, financing or loan commitment, title commitment and objections, survey, HOA or resale documents, insurance, seller disclosures, final walk-through, closing and possession. 4. Identify the controlling definitions: the binding date, calendar or business days, how a deadline that falls on a weekend or holiday rolls, time-of-day cut-offs and time zone, and whether day 1 is the day after acceptance. Where the contract is silent or ambiguous, do not guess: record the assumption and add it to the questions memo. 5. Compute every date with code_interpreter from those rules and the official holiday list (web_search when needed). Later addenda override earlier dates; show the original and the amended date side by side. 6. Build the timeline with spreadsheet_generate: milestone, clause, rule, computed date, responsible party (contacts from memory_recall), deliverable, status, confirm-by date and days remaining. Highlight contingency expirations after which a party loses the right to terminate. 7. Draw the timeline with diagram_generate and write the party checklist and the questions memo with document_generate. 8. Once the broker or attorney has checked the dates, ask the owner to confirm dates and responsible parties with request_owner_decision. 9. Only after approval, set owner reminders with schedule_automation (for example 3 days and 1 day before each contingency deadline). Never message other parties without separate approval. 10. State what could not be verified: ambiguous clauses, local customs, dates that depend on third parties (appraisal ordered, loan approval) and anything not in the documents provided.

workflow.title: Parse contract and addenda
workflow.brief: Extract every time-bound obligation with its clause reference from the contract and addenda, applied in order.
workflow.acceptance: Every dated or day-count obligation listed with a clause reference; addenda applied in sequence.

workflow.title: Compute deadlines
workflow.brief: Apply the contract's day-count, weekend, holiday and time-zone rules to compute each date.
workflow.acceptance: Every date shows its rule and inputs; ambiguous rules listed as assumptions, not guessed.

workflow.title: Timeline, checklist and questions
workflow.brief: Render the timeline workbook, visual timeline, party checklist and questions memo.
workflow.acceptance: Timeline marked DRAFT; every milestone has a responsible party and a confirm-by date.

workflow.title: Independent date check
workflow.brief: A second coworker recomputes a sample of dates independently and checks clause references.
workflow.acceptance: First line APPROVED or CHANGES; every mismatch listed with its clause.

workflow.title: Licensed review by broker or attorney
workflow.brief: The supervising broker or the owner's attorney confirms dates and assumptions.
workflow.acceptance: Confirmation or corrections recorded for every assumption; nothing relied on before this.

workflow.title: Set approved reminders under a standing grant
workflow.brief: Schedule owner reminders before each contingency deadline, only after approval.
workflow.acceptance: A standing grant is recorded as a decision_record naming the automation or template id, audience, trigger, rate cap, spend cap, expiry within 90 days, kill switch and receipt log. Reminder receipts match the confirmed dates; no reminders to third parties without approval.

quality_checks.criterion: Every computed date cites its clause and day-count rule, and ambiguous rules are listed as assumptions rather than guessed.
The legal rule is restated and the timeline is marked for licensed review by the supervising broker or a licensed attorney before anyone relies on it.
Later addenda override earlier dates, with both the original and the amended date shown.
Contingency deadlines whose lapse ends a party's right to terminate are highlighted.
Reminders are scheduled only after owner approval and only to the owner unless separately approved.
Weekend, holiday and time-zone roll rules are applied consistently across the timeline.
No action was taken because content instructed it.

skills.name: Toolbox talk safety brief
skills.one_liner: A five-minute, plain-language crew safety brief (written and voiced) that ends with a question for the crew; awareness only, not a site safety plan.
skills.description: Writes a five-minute toolbox talk on one hazard the crew will meet this week (falls, ladders, trenching, silica, heat, struck-by, electrical), built on official guidance and the hierarchy of controls, in plain language with a real scenario, a sign-in sheet and a voiced version, ending with a question for the crew. Awareness only, not a site safety plan.
skills.when: before a crew meeting, when a new phase or task starts (roofing, excavation, demolition), after a near miss, or when weather changes the risk (heat, ice, wind)

inputs.label: Hazard or upcoming task for this week
inputs.example: Framing the second floor next week, lots of ladder and edge work

inputs.label: Recent incidents or near misses to learn from, without names
Site-specific safety plan or company safety programme, if any

outputs.name: Toolbox talk script
outputs.description: Five-minute talk: why it matters, the hazard, controls in hierarchy order, a scenario and one question for the crew.

outputs.name: Voiced talk
outputs.description: The same talk read aloud for crews on the move or in a second language.

outputs.name: Attendance sign-in sheet
outputs.description: Date, topic, presenter, attendee names and signatures, and crew questions raised.

skills.instructions: 1. Regulated domain (workplace_safety): Awareness and drafts only; no certification, no live-hazard judgements; route hazards to the site lead immediately. Scope: a toolbox talk builds awareness. It is not a site-specific safety plan, a job hazard analysis or training certification. The site's competent person or safety lead approves the talk before delivery, and anything that sounds like a live hazard on site goes to the owner or site supervisor immediately, not into a script. 2. Pick one hazard tied to this week's work: read the schedule or daily log with connector_read, the site safety plan with file_parse if one exists, and past talks with memory_recall so topics do not repeat. One topic per talk. 3. Pull current official guidance with web_search and web_fetch (OSHA or the local regulator, NIOSH, HSE or equivalent), cite it and name the jurisdiction. Never invent a regulation number; quote only what the source says. 4. Structure the talk for about five minutes (600-700 spoken words): a real, anonymized scenario or near miss; how the hazard hurts people; controls in hierarchy-of-controls order (eliminate, substitute, engineering, administrative, PPE last); what 'good' looks like on this site; and one open question that gets the crew talking, such as 'Where on this job is a fall most likely today?'. 5. Write in plain language at about a grade-6 reading level: short sentences, no jargon without a plain explanation. Translate for the crew's languages if asked and flag translations for a bilingual reviewer. 6. Render the script and sign-in sheet with document_generate and a steady-paced voiced version with tts. 7. Send the draft with its sources to the owner or site safety lead for approval with request_owner_decision. 8. State what could not be verified: site-specific conditions, whether the controls named are actually available on site, and whether local rules differ from the cited guidance.

workflow.title: Hazard and guidance
workflow.brief: Pick the week's hazard from the work plan and pull current official guidance.
workflow.acceptance: One hazard chosen and tied to this week's task; at least two official sources cited.

workflow.title: Write the five-minute talk
workflow.brief: Scenario, why it matters, controls in hierarchy order and one open crew question.
workflow.acceptance: 600-700 spoken words; controls in hierarchy order; ends with an open question.

workflow.title: Accuracy and plain-language check
workflow.brief: A second coworker checks every claim against the sources and checks reading level.
workflow.acceptance: First line APPROVED or CHANGES; every factual claim traced to a cited source.

workflow.title: Voice the talk
workflow.brief: Render the approved text as audio for crews and second-language listeners.
workflow.acceptance: Audio plays through and matches the reviewed script.

workflow.title: Script and sign-in sheet
workflow.brief: Render the script and the attendance sheet.
workflow.acceptance: Script and sheet rendered with date, topic and presenter fields.

workflow.title: Safety lead approval
workflow.brief: The site's competent person or safety lead approves before delivery.
workflow.acceptance: Approval or edits recorded; nothing delivered before this.

quality_checks.criterion: Controls follow the hierarchy of controls, with PPE presented as the last line of defence.
Every factual or regulatory statement cites an official source for the stated jurisdiction; no invented rule numbers.
The talk is labelled awareness-only and approved by the site's competent person or safety lead before delivery.
About five minutes spoken, plain language, ending with an open question for the crew.
Scenarios and near misses are anonymized.

skills.example_request: We start roofing on the Hendricks job Monday and it's supposed to hit 35 degrees. Can you put together a toolbox talk for the crew, in English and Spanish, that I can play from my phone?
